input:
If y = log(sin x) tan x, then (dy/dx) at x = π/4 has the value

Options:
A. 4/log 2
B. -3 log 2
C. -4/log 2
D. 3 log 2

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Given y = log(sin x)(tan x), i.e., logarithm of tan x with base sin x, find dy/dx and evaluate it at x = π/4.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Use change of base formula to write y = log(tan x)/log(sin x), then differentiate using the quotient rule. At x = π/4, tan(π/4) = 1 so log(1) = 0, which simplifies the numerator.

key_concepts: Change of base: log_a(b) = log b / log a
d/dx[log(tan x)] = sec²x/tan x = 1/(sin x cos x)
d/dx[log(sin x)] = cos x/sin x = cot x

key_formulas.quotient_rule: dy/dx = [log(sin x)·d/dx(log tanx) - log(tan x)·d/dx(log sinx)] / (log sin x)²

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Convert to natural/common log quotient, differentiate using quotient rule, substitute x = π/4 values and simplify.
logical_steps: Step 1: Write y = log(tan x)/log(sin x)
Step 2: Apply quotient rule for dy/dx
Step 3: Substitute x = π/4: tan=1, sin=1/√2, sec²=2, cos=1/√2
Step 4: Note log(tan(π/4)) = log(1) = 0 → second term vanishes
Step 5: Simplify and compute the value

step_2_quotient_rule.numerator: log(sin x)·[sec²x/tan x] - log(tan x)·[cos x/sin x]
step_2_quotient_rule.dy/dx: [log(sin x)·sec²x/tan x - log(tan x)·cot x] / (log sin x)²

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: At x=π/4: log(tanx)=0 kills the second term. Only term: log(1/√2)·2/1 = -log2. Denominator: (log(1/√2))² = (log2/2)² = (log2)²/4. Result: -log2/(log2)²/4 = -4/log2 ✓
